subject: Technical gate & milestone plan for eval — org/API keys, allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@heliomedics.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@heliomedics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical gate & milestone plan for eval — org/API keys, allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Alex / Sanjay,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HelioMedics' use case for near-real-time clinical summarization aligns well with what we see working in production. Per our conversation, I put together a compact technical gate and milestone plan to get the evaluation (2-week pilot) up and running. The goal is to have an env ready for a seeded end-to-end test by Tue 4/22.

High-level next steps (I attached a one-page MAP workbook):
- Org & IAM: create HelioMedics org tenant and a staging service account. We provide a template and can accept service account keys or a cross-account role.
- API keys: we will provision scoped API keys for the pilot (read-only + usage limits) and rotate them after cutover.
- IP allowlist: please provide the egress IP ranges for your firewall (or we can use peering).
- VPC peering: if you want private peering, we need a VPC CIDR and peering contact to start the cloud request (typically 5–7 biz days).

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Do you want public API with allowlist (fastest) or private VPC peering (more secure, longer lead)?
2) Who owns the cloud peering request on your side (name + email)?
3) Any strict RTO/RPO expectations for the pilot?

Requested dates:
- Confirm approach (allowlist vs peering): by EOD Mon 4/14
- Provide IP ranges / peering contact: by Wed 4/16
- Redwood to provision keys & org staging: by Fri 4/18
- End-to-end seeded test: Tue 4/22

I looped Sanjay to help with the peering/network details. Neha (our infra lead) and Marissa (CS lead) are cc'd on the follow-up to coordinate the access window.

Attachments: HelioMedics_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), redwood-network-diagram.png

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps prioritize the items.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful and very clear. We want the pilot to run over private peering if possible (PHI adjacency on our staging), but we understand the lead time. Sanjay will be the peering owner.

Answers:
1) Preference: VPC peering (security team request).
2) Peering owner: Sanjay Rao (sanjay.rao@heliomedics.com), Cloud Eng.
3) RTO: 1 hour, but that's for production. For the pilot we only need test runs and latency profiling — not a formal SLA.

I'll ask security for the CIDR and any compliance pointers and get back by Tuesday. Can you confirm the minimum info you need for the peering request (VPC ID / CIDR / contact / region)? Also, if peering is in play, do we still need an IP allowlist for a temporary path?

Best,
Alex
CTO | HelioMedics
alex.porter@heliomedics.com

Alex / Sanjay — great, thanks for the quick turn. To answer your peering checklist question, at minimum we need:
- customer VPC ID and CIDR, preferred region (e.g., us-west-2), and an email contact for the cloud request
- security contact name for the exchange of network/ACL policies (we can accept a pointer to your IRG ticket)
- whether you want inbound-only peering (Helio calls Redwood endpoints) or full routing (recommended for low-latency KV cache)

If you choose peering, you can skip the long-term IP allowlist — but we recommend a short-term allowlist during initial validation while peering is created.

Internal note: Neha, can you review Redwood's peering playbook and confirm the expected lead time again? I remember 3–7 business days depending on region and cloud provider; flag anything special we should tell Helio.

Marissa, I'll need you to prep a pilot runbook with test payloads and the evaluation checklist (latency, token budget, failure modes, QA prompts).

Jordan

Hey all — looped in here to confirm timelines and technical asks from the infra side. Short answers first:
- Expected peering lead time: 5 business days once we have customer VPC details and approval. Complex org policies can extend to ~10 business days.
- Required info for our request: customer VPC ID, CIDR, region, owner email, and a ticket/reference for any org-level approvals.
- We recommend a temp IP allowlist during ramp (Redwood egress: 3.23.112.0/24, 3.23.113.0/24 — we'll provide final ranges).

For the MAP workbook, we will:
1) Provision a staging tenant and generate two scoped API keys (one for test ingestion, one for eval inference). Keys will be labeled with expiry 30 days.
2) Create an onboarding checklist for port/ACL checks, NAT, and peering acceptance tests (we use an automated script for the BGP/handshake validation).
3) Share a DocuSign link for the peering addendum if Helio requires a legal add-on.

To keep the pilot timeline: please aim to share the VPC CIDR and peering contact by Tue 4/15 EOD; we'll file the peering request Wed 4/16 and target peering completion by Tue 4/22. If Helio can't meet that date, we can still run an allowlist-based validation by 4/18.

Alex — once you have the CIDR, send to me directly and I'll open the cloud request.

Neha Kapoor
